summary: The new hir/abap indent/Format implementation satisfies every acceptance bullet (verified by the patch's tests, independent scratch tests, a 1000-case fuzz for termination/idempotency/255-byte limit/token preservation, and Format over all 80 real .abap files in the repo), and all generated-ABAP producers (EmitNamed, ts.Transpile, llvm Compile/CompileMultiClass, tsfront drivers, wasm wrapLongLines) now route through Format; the full Go test suite passes and the golden-file changes are whitespace-only. Remaining findings are unreachable-from-generators edge cases: a quote character inside a full-line " comment can steal the next statement's indentation level, INTERFACE ... DEFERRED opens a block unlike CLASS ... DEFERRED, and the GET-event heuristic misses the GET node FIELDS ... event form.

findings.claim: A quote byte (', `, |) inside a full-line " comment sets stmt.first for the next statement, so a comment line preceding a dedenting closer (ENDIF/ENDMETHOD/ENDCLASS) is indented at the closer's column instead of the enclosing block's level.
findings.repro:
In package abap: indent("IF a = 1.
" don't do this
ENDIF.
") leaves the comment at column 0 while " it's a note
x = 1. inside the block is indented at 2; a comment without a quote stays at 2. Not reachable from current generators (wasm strips comments; hir/abap emits only '*' comments, which are exempt).

findings.claim: INTERFACE has no DEFERRED/LOAD exemption like the CLASS case, so 'INTERFACE foo DEFERRED.' opens a block that nothing closes and every following line gains two spaces until an ENDINTERFACE appears.
findings.repro: In package abap: indent("INTERFACE lif DEFERRED.\nDATA x TYPE i.\n") returns the DATA line indented at 2 instead of 0. No repo emitter generates deferred interface declarations.

findings.claim: reportEvent only treats the 2/3-word 'GET node [LATE]' forms as report events, so the real event syntax 'GET node FIELDS f1 f2.' is indented inside the previous event instead of starting a new one at column zero.
findings.repro:
In package abap: indent("START-OF-SELECTION.
WRITE 'a'.
GET mara FIELDS matnr.
WRITE 'b'.
") keeps GET/WRITE indented at 2 instead of resetting GET to column 0. Generated reports only use GET RUN TIME / GET TIME STAMP style statements, which are correctly excluded.
